intro.kit.1.text: Dutch calls every day. Dutch calls to tell us the rent is late.

intro.kit.2.text: Real work? Like, paying work? Not “hold this bag and don’t look inside” work?

intro.rook.3.text: The Drowned Saint. Ten minutes. And eat something first. Nobody punches well on an empty stomach.

intro.kit.3.text: Hungry’s fine. Hungry’s how I win.

intro.narrate.1.text: Rook takes his coat from the hook the slow way, keeping his left side still.

intro.kit.4.text: Doc Yun said three weeks off. It’s been one.

intro.rook.4.text: Then I’m two weeks ahead. The ribs are fine. It’s the wiring that’s sulking.

plaza.rustfang_punk.1.text: Well, well. Rook’s little stray. Nice jacket. Bet it looks better on me.

plaza.kit.1.text: Bet it looks better on you when you’re not face down in a puddle.

plaza.rook.1.text: Two Rustfangs. Try not to show off.

plaza.rook.2.text: Sloppy. You dropped your guard twice.

plaza.rook.3.text: You beat Rustfangs. That’s like beating the weather. Come on.

plaza.narrate.1.text: He says it with a hand pressed flat to his side, where he thinks she can’t see.

saint.dutch.again_sable.text: Whoever that is with you, darlin’, I never saw him. I never saw any of you.

saint.dutch.again.text: The meter’s running on Mr. Pale’s patience. Go find your jockey.

saint.dutch.1.text: There they are. My favorite disaster and his apprentice. Sit, sit. Mind the stain, it’s load-bearing.

saint.dutch.2.text: This is Mr. Pale. He represents, let’s say, an interested party.

saint.narrate.1.text: Mr. Pale is peeling a satsuma with a small folding knife. The peel comes away in one unbroken spiral. He never looks at his hands.

saint.pale.1.text: A pleasure. I’ll be brief; I bill by the minute. Under the flooded Sinkline there is a sealed research annex. Kessler-Mori wrote it off after the flood of ’61.

saint.pale.2.text: Inside is a {y}data core{/}. Bring it to me intact and you will be paid {y}three thousand cred{/}.

saint.rook.2.text: A written-off annex. A milk run. You could send anybody. Why us?

saint.pale.3.text: Because “anybody” asks more questions. Also, the annex doors are still corporate-locked. You will need a deck jockey.

saint.dutch.3.text: Which you haven’t got, since your last one moved to Neo-Lagos and stopped taking my calls.

saint.dutch.4.text: Hex! Hex owes me money. Two birds, one run. Tell them if they do this, their tab goes in the canal.

saint.pale.4.text: Expenses. I will not be asking for receipts.

saint.pale.5.text: Loading Dock 7, when you have it. I keep very exact hours.

saint.pale.6.text: Miss Kit. Those two Rustfangs outside: nine seconds, no weapon, no chrome in those hands. I watched from the window.

saint.pale.7.text: So nothing. I collect numbers. That one is unusual.

saint.rook.4.text: She’s not part of the price.

saint.pale.8.text: Of course not, Mr. Rook. Prices are for things one pays for.

saint.narrate.2.text: He splits the satsuma, counts the segments under his breath, and leaves it on the table uneaten. He is gone before the door finishes swinging.

saint.dutch.5.text: Does that every time. Never eats one. Don’t ask.

saint.dutch.6.text: Word of advice? Get paid before you get proud.

saint.dutch.7.text: I know, darlin’. That’s why I said it to you and not him. Oh, and if you need pocket money, the {c}job board{/} by the door always has something.

hexden.hex.1.text: Is that— is that a Stingray? Don’t drop it. Please don’t drop it. Slowly. Give it here slowly.

hexden.hex.2.text: No. You do it. My hands are shaking. Pins to pins, then the clips. I’ll talk you through it.

hexden.narrate.1.text: Hex’s deck runs a new program: {y}Overload{/}, a surge that fries machines. Their deck’s under {c}Deck{/} in the menu now.

hexden.hex.4.text: Rook. Sit. Your reflex wiring’s been double-firing since you walked in. I can hear it clicking. Chrome shouldn’t click.

hexden.narrate.2.text: Hex runs a cable from the deck to the port behind Rook’s ear. Thirty seconds of scrolling numbers. Something in his shoulder stops twitching.

hexden.tuned.text: Rook’s chrome is re-tuned: {y}{unlocked}{/} are back, and his wound costs him less.

hexden.hex.6.text: Your side’s still a mess, though. That’s meat. I don’t do meat.

hexden.hex.7.text: Okay. A deal’s a deal. I’m already regretting it. Let’s go rob a haunted subway.

hexden.hex.8.text: Also, my emergency fund. It’s mostly been emergencies.

hexden.hex.9.text: One more thing. I run a scanner, {c}Analyze{/}. Feed its target data into Rook’s smartgun and he literally cannot miss. I call it {y}Target Lock{/}. Patent pending.

hexden.hex.10.text: Rustyard. Old Mags. Stingray, the one with the little fin logo. I’ll be here. Checking the door locks. Twice.

hexden.hex.11.text: I didn’t do it. Whatever it is. Oh— it’s you. Hi, Rook. Hi, Rook’s kid.

hexden.kit.1.text: Kit. My name’s been Kit for nineteen years.

hexden.rook.2.text: We have a job. Corporate doors, down in the Sinkline.

hexden.hex.13.text: No. Absolutely not. Also I can’t: my deck’s dead. Fried the coprocessor on an all-nighter. A hobby. Look at her. She’s crying.

hexden.hex.14.text: With what cred? A Stingray costs more than this building. Which I also owe money on.

hexden.hex.16.text: Some is a number. I can work with a number. There’s a scavver in the Rustyard, {y}Old Mags{/}. She had a Stingray last month. Rustyard’s east, past the Barrens. Get me that chip and I’m your jockey. Your professional, sober deck jockey.

hexden.hex.17.text: The Barrens are nasty. Here, I can spare these.

gate.mags.1.text: Off my lot. Forty years I’ve held this yard against worse than you, and I’m still counting.

gate.rustfang_punk.1.text: Knuckles says this yard pays tribute now, grandma. Hounds! Fetch.

gate.rustfang_punk.2.text: Knuckles is gonna hear about this! He’s gonna feed you to the hounds!

gate.mags.2.text: Hmph. Didn’t need help. Didn’t mind it, either. What do you want?

gate.mags.3.text: Ha! Had one. Knuckles’ boys took it, along with half my stock. Hauled it all up to the old {y}tire depot{/} at the north end of the yard.

gate.mags.4.text: You do that and the chip’s yours. Plus a discount at my counter. Deal’s a deal.

knuckles.knuckles_tran.1.text: So these are the heroes. Know what I do to heroes? I charge ’em rent.

knuckles.knuckles_tran.2.text: Ugh… fine… take your junk… I’m moving to Neo-Lagos…

knuckles.knuckles_tran.3.text: Your fixer’s got a big mouth, y’know. Whole yard knew you were hunting a deck jockey before you did.

knuckles.kit.1.text: Dutch talks. That’s not the same as selling us.

knuckles.kit.2.text: The crate. Mags’ stuff should be in there.

rustyard.mags.1.text: Tire depot, north end. Knuckles is the big one with the chrome hands. Can’t miss him. Wish I could.

rustyard.mags.2.text: Well, well. Knuckles is limping all the way to Neo-Lagos, I hear. Here. As promised.

rustyard.mags.3.text: Our water filter was in that crate too. The little ones have been drinking canal for a month.

rustyard.kit.1.text: We found the camp’s tribute as well. Behind the tagged heap. It’s yours.

rustyard.mags.4.text: Keep it. Where you’re going you’ll need it more than we will. The camp voted. I counted.

rustyard.mags.fork.text: And this. The camp took up a collection for whoever ran Knuckles off: {y}150¢{/}. Don’t argue with me, I’m old.

rustyard.mags.kept_kit.text: Keep it. The little ones need it more than our rent does.

rustyard.mags.kept_reply.text: Hmph. Then here’s what it buys you: anything on my lot, a fifth off. For as long as I’m breathing.

rustyard.mags.7.text: And tell Hex they still owe me for the last one.

rustyard.mags.menu.text: Shopping? The crew that ran Knuckles off my lot gets fair prices. For once.

rustyard.mags.9.text: The Sinkline? Flooded in ’61, whole trains still down there. Things live in the water now. Big things. Bring fire. Or a bigger thing.

sinkline.narrate.1.text: A transit-authority service gate. The lock panel blinks {r}LOCKED{/}: corporate encryption.

sinkline.rook.1.text: This is what the jockey’s for.

sinkline.hex.1.text: Transit authority lock with Kessler-Mori wrapping. Cute. Give me a second.

sinkline.hex.2.text: Done. Welcome to the Sinkline. Mind the gap. Mind the ghosts. Mind the everything.

crew.narrate.1.text: Three bodies in expensive gear, slumped against the platform. Whatever got them wasn’t a ghoul. Their wounds are cauterized.

crew.hex.1.text: That’s the {c}Glass Wolves{/}. Runners out of Harbor Ward. Good ones.

crew.narrate.2.text: One of them clutches a data slate. The last message reads: {c}“Dutch set it up. Milk run. In and out.”{/}

crew.rook.1.text: Same job. Different crew. Before us. And he sat there and poured us drinks and didn’t say a word.

crew.hex.2.text: Maybe he didn’t know they didn’t come back.

crew.rook.2.text: Dutch knows everything that happens below the canal. That’s what he sells.

crew.narrate.3.text: A cred stick in the leader’s jacket, still warm with charge.

crew.rook.4.text: They’d want it spent on the job that killed them. Take it.

pump.open.text: {intake}, open. The gauge sits steady at {c}{psi} psi{/}.

pump.hex.1.text: Hold on. Before anybody cranks a random wheel: this is one of the pump intakes. The pump room console should say how they want opening. South, off the platform.

pump.wheel.text: {intake}: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}{psi} psi{/}.

pump.grinds.text: The wheel grinds round. Water hisses into {intake}, and somewhere across the level a pipe knocks in answer.

pump.narrate.1.text: The last wheel turns. Every pipe in the room drums once, then settles into a low, even hum.

pump.hex.2.text: Pressure’s balanced and the pumps are primed. Now the console in the pump room.

pump.bang_spins.text: {r}BANG.{/} A pressure kick hammers down the line, and {intake}’s wheel spins shut again.

pump.bang_stuck.text: {r}BANG.{/} A pressure kick hammers down the line. The wheel won’t budge.

pump.hex.order_seen.text: Okay. Order matters. Lowest pressure first, and that means reading all three gauges before we touch anything. I did say that. Out loud.

pump.hex.order_unseen.text: Okay. Order matters. There’s a right order, and the pump console in the pump room knows it. Let’s go ask it.

floodgate.narrate.1.text: The pump console hums. Water levels: {g}NOMINAL{/}.

floodgate.narrate.2.text:
The pump console flickers awake: {r}INTAKES DRY.{/} {c}PRIME: OPEN INTAKES 1–3, LOWEST PRESSURE FIRST.{/}
Intake 1: platform track bed · Intake 2: service bay · Intake 3: this station.

floodgate.hex.1.text: Three intakes, all over the level. We read every gauge first. Then we open them lowest to highest. Nobody touches a wheel before that. Please.

floodgate.hex.2.text: Pump control. Still got power, somehow. If I spin up the drainage pumps, the junction should empty out.

floodgate.kit.1.text: And whatever lives in the junction?

floodgate.hex.3.text: Will be a lot easier to see coming. Best I can do from a pump console.

floodgate.narrate.3.text: Across the level, pumps groan to life. The black water in the junction falls away, and a catwalk rises out of it.

lurker.kit.1.text: The water— it’s moving on its own.

lurker.hex.1.text: That is not water. That is a LOT of teeth.

lurker.hex.2.text: Maintenance shaft past the junction goes down. The annex should be under us.

annexdoor.narrate.1.text: A pressure door marked {c}K-M ANNEX 7 · AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL{/}. The lock wants a physical passkey.

annexdoor.hex.1.text: Hardware key. I can’t crack a chunk of plastic. Somebody down here has one.

guards.k_m_sentinel.1.text: Contact! Unauthorized personnel in Annex 7! Lethal response authorized!

guards.narrate.1.text: One of the Sentinels wears a passkey on a lanyard. Hex lifts it off him with two fingers.

guards.hex.1.text: One chunk of plastic, acquired. Told you somebody down here had one.

guards.hex.2.text: Huh. The door log has us in it. “Contractor team, due the 14th. Status: pending resolution.” That’s a weird word for a door to use.

guards.rook.1.text: Active security in an abandoned lab. Pale lied.

guards.hex.3.text: Pale lied, the lab lied, the lights are lying. I read systems for a living, and nothing down here will tell me the truth.

lattice.look.text:
A security lattice: three emitters, beams humming across the passage. Three cables climb its frame, amber, green and violet, each tapping into some of the emitters.
Emitters: {emitters}

lattice.hex.1.text: Can’t hack a laser. But lasers need power, and power comes through relays. Find the relays.

relay.down.text: {relay}. The lattice is down; nothing left to route.

relay.hex.1.text: Security relay. I can cycle it, but I can’t see what it feeds from here. Only one way to find out.

relay.narrate.1.text: Down the hall, the laser lattice stutters, flickers, and dies.

relay.hex.2.text: Lattice is down! Turns out I can lie to a lab too.

relay.clunk.text: The relay clunks over. Lattice emitters: {emitters}

cryopod.narrate.1.text: A cryopod, humming, lit from within. Frost on the glass. Behind it, a figure: an orc, bone-white hair, eyes closed.

cryopod.hex.1.text: Label reads {c}ASSET S-7 · “VESSEL” · SPARK YIELD 94%{/}. Oh no. Oh no no no.

cryopod.hex.2.text: This is the data core. It’s not data. It’s a person.

cryopod.rook.2.text: Kit. Three thousand cred, the rent, Hex’s debt—

cryopod.kit.2.text: Nine seconds. Pale timed me in the street and wrote it down.

cryopod.kit.3.text: That’s how you end up in there, Rook. Somebody likes your numbers.

cryopod.rook.4.text: Twenty years ago I stood in a lab like this. Different logo. My crew got paid, and I walked out past a tank with somebody still in it.

cryopod.rook.5.text: I told myself it wasn’t my job. I’ve been telling myself that every night since.

cryopod.rook.6.text: Do it, kid. Whatever it costs.

cryopod.rook.7.text: You never needed to carry it. Now you do. Go on.

cryopod.hex.3.text: For the record, I hate “whatever it costs.” I’m doing it anyway.

cryopod.narrate.2.text: Kit’s hand touches the glass, and something in her answers. Ki surges up through her arm like a struck match. Frost blooms, cracks, and shatters.

cryopod.sable.1.text: …The crow was screaming. For so long. Now it’s quiet.

cryopod.kit.6.text: Started last month. I don’t know why.

cryopod.sable.3.text: Mm. The crow says you’re loud. That’s not an insult.

cryopod.sable.4.text: I am Sable. I don’t know how long I was in there. They took— they took a lot. I still have enough.

cryopod.rook.8.text: We’ll get you out of here. After that you owe us nothing.

cryopod.sable.5.text: Everyone who opened this glass said something kind. The crow remembers each of them.

cryopod.sable.7.text: There were others. S-5. S-6. The pods beside mine went dark, one night and then another. Nobody wrote down where they went.

cryopod.hex.4.text: Somebody did. It’s in the pod logs.

cryopod.narrate.3.text: Hex jacks into the pod’s panel. For a long minute the only sound is the deck, copying: intake dates, yields, transfer orders. Every name.

cryopod.hex.5.text: Got it. All of it. It goes wherever we go, and it doesn’t go to Pale.

cryopod.sable.8.text: …Then I will walk with you. As far as the door. After that I will decide.

cryopod.narrate.4.text: Hex puts their jacket round Sable’s shoulders. Rook watches the door. Nobody says anything about three thousand cred.

cryopod.narrate.5.text: Kit falls in beside Rook. She doesn’t ask about the other tank, and he doesn’t offer. Their shoulders touch, once, on the way to the door.

cryopod.sable.9.text: You. The old one. You’re bleeding under that coat.

cryopod.sable.10.text: The crow doesn’t care how old it is. Hold still.

cryopod.narrate.6.text: Sable lays two fingers against Rook’s side. Something black-feathered and warm passes through the room. When he steps back, the stitches are just a scar.

cryopod.mended.text: Rook’s wound is closed: full strength, every charge back, and {y}{mended}{/} too.

cryopod.kit.8.text: Don’t get used to it. You still owe Doc Yun for the stitches.

cryopod.narrate.7.text: {r}ALERT. ASSET S-7 CONTAINMENT BREACH. WARDEN PROTOCOL ENGAGED.{/}

cryopod.hex.6.text: WARDEN protocol. That sounds big. Things named “Warden” are always big.

cryopod.rook.11.text: Freight lift. South, through the containment door. Move.

cryopod.hex.7.text: One stop first: that armory by the hall had weapon cases. Whatever WARDEN is, I want to meet it holding something better.

warden.narrate.1.text: The floor shudders. A security platform unfolds from the wall, three meters of plate and cannon. Something inside its chest glows and screams.

warden.sable.1.text: There’s a spirit in its heart. Bound. Starving. It was one of us once.

warden.rook.1.text: Then we set it free. Crew, on me.

warden.narrate.2.text: The spirit rises from the wreck, no longer screaming. It circles Sable once, like a bird, and fades into the pipes.

warden.sable.2.text: It thanked you. It said its name. I won’t repeat it; it was only for us.

warden.rook.2.text: Not this time. That’s all I wanted.

warden.sable.3.text: The crow has gone up the lift shaft ahead of us. It sees farther than I can.

warden.sable.4.text: Cars at the top. People waiting in the rain.

warden.rook.3.text: Pale’s pickup. He did say he keeps exact hours.

warden.hex.1.text: The lift’s live. Let’s never come back here.

betrayal.narrate.1.text: Mr. Pale is waiting under the cranes, peeling a satsuma. The spiral of peel hangs from his knife, unbroken.

betrayal.pale.1.text: Three minutes early. I do appreciate punctuality in a liability.

betrayal.pale.2.text: Asset S-7 is Kessler-Mori property, recovered from a site we officially abandoned by deniable contractors.

betrayal.pale.5.text: I did tell you I collect numbers, Miss Kit. I have already sold yours.

betrayal.narrate.2.text: He splits the satsuma and counts the segments under his breath. Eleven.

betrayal.pale.6.text: Contractors are paid on completion. You have completed.

betrayal.pale.7.text: Except you, Miss Kit. The Vessel program is always short of subjects.

betrayal.narrate.3.text: The peel drops to the wet concrete. One unbroken spiral.

betrayal.k_m_sentinel.1.text: Contractor tags read. Four signatures. One flagged for intake, three for disposal.

betrayal.act.text: Rifles come up all along the dock.
choices: Get in front of Hex and Sable

betrayal.narrate.5.text: Kit is across the gap before she has decided to be. A Sentinel’s rifle butt meets her halfway, and the concrete meets her after that.

betrayal.pale.8.text: Nine seconds in the street, Miss Kit. You were faster when nobody was watching.

betrayal.narrate.6.text: Kit plants herself in front of Hex and Sable, fists up, burning. The crow screams from a crane. Every red dot on the dock finds her chest.

betrayal.rook.2.text: Kit. When I say run, you run. You don’t look back, you don’t wait for me.

betrayal.narrate.7.text: Rook’s hand comes out of his coat with something small and round in it. The pin is already gone.
